design: moe-kernels-work 2026-10-26 build-C3 (CHECK.md, DESIGN.md; offline, read-only over the repo at e324867c); the owner's option (b) of 2026-10-22 (moe-kernels-work 2026-10-22 refit4/ROUND2.md section 5): one short instrumented rental measuring per-CTA launch and finish times for Mixtral-8x7B and Qwen2-57B, w1 and w2, at vLLM's 128x128x64 w8 s3 G 1 tile, after refit4's two offline rounds failed their gate (REFIT.md, ROUND2.md: Mixtral-8x7B's 128 G 1 w1 runs about 4% faster than priced under every knee form, and C5's theta_L is SEEN-FITTED at 0.25 to 0.30)

gate.not_read_bound: C3-R1 and C3-R2 are NOT READ when, over the read GEMM's cells (Mixtral-8x7B w2), the median of the cells' |median overhead| exceeds 10% or any cell's |worst burst pair| exceeds 20% (read_c3.overhead_ok; two-sided, review MINOR-1: a copy faster than the plain kernel is a compile effect too)
gate.not_read_bound_why: theta_L and g are ratios of a launch spread to a lifetime. A slowdown that scales the whole CTA (a slower main loop, the compile effect rentals 4 and 5 saw) scales the spread and the lifetime alike and leaves them unchanged; a fixed per-CTA cost c lengthens the lifetime only, so at overhead o they read low by at most 1 / (1 + o); a whole-CTA slowdown leaves theta unbiased only when the finish spread scales with L, and reads it low by the same 1 / (1 + o) when the spread is fixed in ns, so the bias lies in [1 / (1 + o), 1] either way (it reads high only under a cost that is not uniform across CTAs). C3-R1's IN band is 0.275 +- 9%: at o = 10% a true 0.275 reads 0.250, IN's edge, and no worse than NEAR up to o = 37%; C3-R2's cut at g 0.5 separates C5's same-wave 0.25 to 0.30 from M4's 1 at any o up to 80% (1 / 1.8 > 0.5). The theta band binds, so the median cap is 10%. The worst-pair cap, 20%, allows burst noise around a median under 10% but voids a page whose cost is far from uniform across bursts, where order could move. A stamped-against-plain launch-order test is not possible: the plain kernel carries no stamps
gate.on_fail: owner OD-1 (2026-10-26; changes decision 2's refuse-on-fail for C3 only): a gate that fails on its TIMING legs alone (median |r - 1| over 1% or worst over 2%) keeps the stamps units; their pages are labelled PERTURBED (stamps.json page_label) and every reading carries the measured overhead (perturb.json per (cell, GEMM): overhead_median = median copy / median plain - 1 and overhead_worst = the worst burst pair). The HARD legs still refuse the unit (gate.env HARD_<id>): CTAs per SM identical, the all-off copy's SASS equal to the plain kernel's, the upstream file, C3's SASS legs (a clock read before the first LDG, none inside the HGMMA loop); and regcheck (CTAs per SM, the wgmma path) must PASS
gate.perturbed_readings: C3-R1 (theta_L) and C3-R2 (the re-read launch gap) are ORDERING quantities: read on PERTURBED pages with the overhead disclosed, unless the read GEMM's overhead passes the NOT-READ bound. C3-R3 (the w1 LIFE / PACKING split) is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY on PERTURBED pages: printed, never used to price or select a model form
gate.perturbed_theta: review MINOR-2 and MINOR-3: on PERTURBED pages theta and theta (1 + o) are both printed (o the w2 median |overhead|) and the band is reported only when both fall in one band, else '<band> or <band> (PERTURBED)'; a PERTURBED theta_L is never registered as MEASURED: at most MEASURED-PERTURBED, and a later round may use it only as such. Any theta_L C3 reads on Mixtral-8x7B is IN-SAMPLE for Mixtral-8x7B in any later held-out round
gate.reference: the perturb unit's plain-kernel medians are C3's uninstrumented reference: C3-R3's e_plain and the stamped-over-plain cost are read against them
gate.regcheck: compile only, before any timed unit: the all-off copy and the stamped copy at the plain kernel's CTAs per SM, and the plain kernel and the copy on the wgmma path (instr_probe_c3.regcheck_c3)
gate.rule: owner decision 2 (2026-10-06) with rental 5's occupancy leg, on EVERY C3 cell: per (cell, GEMM) r = median plain ms / median copy ms over 8 alternating bursts of 10 calls each way; PASS iff median |r - 1| <= 1% and worst <= 2%, CTAs per SM identical per config, the all-off copy's SASS equal to the plain kernel's (line info stripped), the installed fused_moe.py the upstream file, and C3's SASS legs on every stamped config: a clock read before the first LDG and none inside the k-loop (the back-branch spanning the most HGMMA; instr_probe_c3.sass_checks_c3)

instrument.copy: moe/instrumented/fused_moe_instr.py (vLLM v0.27.1 fused_moe_kernel plus rental 4's approved stamps)
instrument.flush: before every stamped call: the stamp buffers allocated, the GPU held ahead by instr_probe's 25 ms sleep (review MAJOR-2, as the burst timer does, so no launch waits on the host), then an L2 flush outside the launch event pair
instrument.kept_per_launch: the int64 rows, expert_ids and num_tokens_post_padded vLLM handed the launch (references held, copied to the host after the call's synchronize), USE_TD (must be False), the launch's event-pair ms
instrument.span: each launch's stamp_span_ns (first live start to last live end, globaltimer) is recorded beside its event-pair ms; the reader prints event / span per cell
instrument.spec: stamps=ends,evict_a=none,evict_b=none (STAMPS 3: CTA start before the dead check, a dead CTA's exit, the end after the final store; nothing near the wgmma k-loop)

priced.generator: moe-kernels-work 2026-10-26 build-C3/work/priced_c3.py (offline, read-only; run from refit4/work)
priced.what: the priced 128 G 1 GEMM times of C3's cells (A2's E1-CAL cells, NATIVE): refit4 ROUND2's selected knee K1 (triad rate 3726.2 GB/s, p and S0) and the null knee N0 (carried bw 3597.8 GB/s, p), each at its LOMO constants with the priced model held out (knee2r.json), on counted bytes of the board's own b128g1 counter page (Mixtral-8x7B: C2's; Qwen2-57B: A2's), dead CTAs included; meas_ms is that page's counted GEMM time (cycles / 1400.8 MHz, the rows' own conversion)

C3-R1.band: IN [0.25, 0.30]; NEAR [0.20, 0.35] outside IN; OUT otherwise

meaning.IN: C5 MEASURED: the launch spread C5 fitted (0.25 to 0.30) is the measured one. A next byte-law round may carry C5's distance with theta_L at the measured value as a MEASURED constant (MEASURED-PERTURBED, and usable only as such, when read on PERTURBED pages); it is IN-SAMPLE for Mixtral-8x7B in any later held-out round (read off that model's own w2); its w1 guard still applies (C5 failed it through M4's soft slab survival, which this does not touch)
meaning.NEAR: C5's mechanism holds and its constant moves: the measured value replaces the SEEN fit in any next round (MEASURED; MEASURED-PERTURBED on PERTURBED pages, usable only as such; in-sample for Mixtral-8x7B), and C5's held-out w2 means are re-priced at it before anything is selected
meaning.NOT READ: no valid Mixtral-8x7B w2 launch: C5 stays SEEN-FITTED
meaning.OUT: the jitter picture is not the launch: C5's 0.25 to 0.30 absorbs something else. C5 stays SEEN-FITTED and cannot be argued from launch physics; a next byte law starts from the measured launch times

C3-R1.read_by: read_c3.launch_reading via wave_theta; model_reading (median over launches)
C3-R1.rule: per w2 launch, each wave k >= 1 of W_c = 264 live ranks with at least 132 CTAs: least squares start_ns = a + s u / W_c (u = r - k W_c), theta_k = s / L, L the launch's median live lifetime; the launch's theta the CTA-weighted mean; theta_L the median over the model's valid w2 launches
C3-R1.what: theta_L, C5's launch spread of a later wave (refit4 DECLARED.txt AM2), on Mixtral-8x7B w2

meaning.LAUNCH-TOGETHER: most re-reads launch within half of M4's staggered gap of their partner, as C3 and C5 assume and the schedule's 82 to 88% says: M4's staggered distance is the wrong picture for Mixtral w2 at 128x128, and a next byte law prices the launch gap, not the rank distance
meaning.MIXED: neither picture: a next byte law prices the measured share directly
meaning.STAGGERED: most re-reads launch about one staggered gap behind their partner, M4's picture: M4's w2 over-prediction is then its survival law's, not its distance's

C3-R2.read_by: read_c3.pairs, same_wave, gap_ratio (launch_reading); pooled in model_reading
C3-R2.rule: a re-read is live rank r whose M-tile pid_m - 1 holds the same expert (expert_ids as vLLM passed the launch); g = (start(r) - start(r - P)) / (P L / W_c), P = N / 128 (M4's staggered gap is 1, C5's same-wave pair theta_L, C3's synchronized wave 0); the banded share (review MAJOR-1): g < 0.5 over the re-reads in waves k >= 1 that the schedule puts in their partner's wave, floor(r / W_c) = floor((r - P) / W_c) (wave 0 launches together under every picture; C5 and C3 read 1.000, M4 0.000), pooled over the model's valid w2 launches whose globaltimer resolution is at most a quarter of P L / W_c (review MINOR-4); the all-pairs share and the schedule share printed beside (DESCRIPTIVE; REFIT.md's 82 to 88% is the schedule_note's)
C3-R2.what: the share of w2 slab re-reads launched with their partner, Mixtral-8x7B

C3-R3.band: on Mixtral-8x7B w1 under K1: NOT REPRODUCED when e_plain < +2%; DESCRIPTIVE ONLY when the w1 overhead (the median over cells of |o|) exceeds a quarter of e_plain; else LIFE when the life share >= 2/3, PACKING <= 1/3, BOTH between; on PERTURBED pages DESCRIPTIVE ONLY whatever the band (owner OD-1)

meaning.BOTH: both terms carry the miss: a next form needs a rate term and a packing term, declared separately
meaning.DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: the w1 overhead (absolute) is over a quarter of this board's plain-kernel miss: the overhead-corrected split is printed and attributes nothing (owner, 2026-10-26)
meaning.LIFE: Mixtral-8x7B's w1 CTAs themselves run faster than priced: the next knee form needs a per-CTA rate term that Mixtral w1 carries and Qwen2 w1 does not (cycles domain), not a wave or launch term
meaning.NOT REPRODUCED: this board's plain kernel does not reproduce the w1 miss (under +2%): the decomposition is printed, nothing is attributed
meaning.PACKING: the CTAs live as priced and the GEMM is shorter than its waves of median lives: the next round declares a time-domain launch-overlap or tail-packing term (C5's jitter physics applied to time)

C3-R3.rule: per cell T_pred = K1 at its LOMO constants (refit4 ROUND2's selected knee; N0 printed beside), registered by value; L_pred = T_pred W_c / live; T_stamp the stamped launch's event-pair time (median over calls; each call held ahead), L_med its median live lifetime (globaltimer); ln(T_pred / T_stamp) = ln(L_pred / L_med) [LIFE] + ln(live L_med / (W_c T_stamp)) [PACKING], exactly; owner 2026-10-26 (review MAJOR-3): LIFE and the total are corrected for the cell's measured w1 overhead o (L and T_stamp over 1 + o; PACKING unchanged; the raw terms printed beside); per model the means over cells; life share = mean LIFE / mean total (read when |mean total| >= 0.005); e_plain = mean T_pred / T_plain - 1 over the cells, T_plain the perturb unit's plain median on the same cell
C3-R3.what: why Mixtral-8x7B's 128 G 1 w1 runs faster than priced: per-CTA life against packing

C3-R4.rule: NOT READ unless: the board valid (read_c2.board: C2_POWER_W=700, LOCK_PROBE_1410=held, G-BAND PASS); the variant's regcheck line and the gate's HARD line PASS (a timing FAIL alone reads PERTURBED, owner OD-1), the page's label the gate's; every stamped config passes C3's SASS legs; the page's histogram is the registered file; and per launch every row stamped live or dead, the live CTAs exactly the pids under (num_tokens_post_padded / 128) x P, USE_TD False, late_buffers 0 (review MINOR-7), 132 distinct SMs, the globaltimer resolution (the least positive difference of distinct start stamps) at most L / 10: a 1.024 us timer still admits every C3 GEMM, whose CTAs live about 20 us and longer at 1410 MHz

schedule_note.derivation: 128 G 1 w2, GROUP_SIZE_M 1: pid = pid_m P + pid_n with P = N / 128 (8x7B 4096 / 128 = 32; 8x22B 6144 / 128 = 48); expert e owns ceil(c_e / 128) consecutive M-tiles (moe_align_block_size, experts ascending), c_e the cell's NATIVE rows per expert (the histogram's counts; balanced: T top_k / E). A re-read is live rank r whose M-tile pid_m - 1 holds the same expert (its partner r - P read the same B slab); it is same-wave when floor(r / 264) = floor((r - P) / 264), W_c = 132 SMs x 2 CTAs. 8x7B uniform and balanced n 2: 2 tiles per expert, 16 tiles, 512 live, 256 re-reads (the second tile of each expert); only r in [264, 295] crosses, pid_m 9, pid_n 0 to 7: 8 pairs, 248 / 256 = 0.969. 8x7B PT (tiles 2,2,3,2,3,3,2,3) and PW (4,3,2,1,3,2,2,3): 20 tiles, 640 live, 384 re-reads, 40 cross: 0.896. Restricted to waves k >= 1 the shares are 0.815 to 0.938. read_c3.pairs and same_wave compute these on every page from the expert_ids vLLM handed the launch
schedule_note.statement: OD-4 (owner, 2026-10-26): refit4 REFIT.md section 2a's 'a re-read P = 32 or 48 ranks behind its partner falls in the same wave for 82 to 88% of pairs' does NOT reproduce for Mixtral-8x7B on C3's cells: the schedule share is 0.896 (PT, PW) and 0.969 (uniform, balanced), pooled 0.925. Mixtral-8x22B's C2 cells give 0.812 to 0.900 (pooled 0.844), so the quoted range matches 8x22B's cells, not 8x7B's. It enters no band
